recs.b: The city, the window, the lab and the stage play as one unbroken camera move, with no hard cuts. Award juries reward continuity, and it feels like a film, not a website.
Higgsfield films of the city, window and lab, turned into image sequences that scrub with your scroll, the way Apple's product pages do. It looks real and expensive, not like a cartoon of a lab.
Your approved gold-chrome liquid glass is the window's rim, with raindrop lenses on the glass that slide away as the glass parts like an iris. This is the signature moment people screenshot.

recs.t: A REAL 3D VIAL ON THE PLINTH
recs.b: A real 3D model of Grace's vial (generated from photos, or a photoreal turntable film) turns slowly on a lit plinth, with real reflections. Never a drawn bottle.
After the first answer, the site's glow follows the visitor's focus colour everywhere: buttons, rails, the vial. It feels personal without saying so.
Eight saturated jewel colours spread around the colour wheel, with bloom and a light pool under each vial. Big, free-standing, no boxes, and only one lit at a time.
The peptides glide past slowly and steadily as you scroll. Each one lights up at centre stage with its focus tags underneath. Arrow keys and swipe work too.
In the lab, the peptide forms as a chain of glass beads, spins, and chrome gyroscope rings orbit it while the camera pushes through. This is the scene people share.
Your cursor carries a soft light across the city glass and the lab bench. Small, but it makes everything feel alive.
Type a lot number and an elegant certificate card resolves. Trust becomes an interaction, and it's a strong award detail too.
A beautifully designed newsletter with an issue preview on the site and a short founder letter from Grace. It's the main lead magnet.
A slim glass bar docked at the bottom edge, in the site's own type: no bubble, no pill, no 'Ask the guide'. Expert concierge voice, with vetted answers from the peptide-expert skill.
Off by default, with a small toggle: a soft city hum, a single drop, a glass ring as the window opens. Juries love it when it's tasteful and optional.
Moving between pages, the vial flies to its new spot (shared-element view transitions), so the site feels like one object.
All-caps headlines in a variable font that subtly widens and tightens as you scroll into each section.
Vertical versions of each scene for phones, so the phone gets its own cinematic cut, not a squashed desktop.
Skip at any moment, a full calm version for reduced motion, a keyboard-operable tour, and fast loading (Lighthouse 90+). This is a scoring category, not just good manners.
A case-study page, a 30-second reel and credits, submitted to Awwwards, CSSDA and FWA once it's live.
Every scene and effect gets a catalogue code (SCN-, LAB-, VIA-) and goes into the APEX library, so it becomes a template other clients can buy.
Privacy-safe events (scroll depth, tour started and finished, which hook converts), so we tune the hooks with real numbers after launch.

plan.b: You read the prompt, tick the hooks and recommendations you want, and say yes. Nothing is built before this.

Peptide skills finished and checked; a PROJECT.md for PEPTICITY; design tokens (ink, ivory/bone, 8 jewel hues, gold-chrome); content map; the lawyer switch carried over; placeholders for Grace's details.

Photoreal stills and films: the ivory city, the gold-chrome window with raindrops, six lab beats, the vial turntable or 3D model, and the jewel-lit vials. Credits needed: films cost far more than stills, and the balance is about 462 credits today, so a top-up is likely. Exact cost confirmed with you before any films.
Scenes 0 to 2 built and verified on desktop and phone, then sent to you as pictures and a link.
The six lab beats, scroll-scrubbed, with captions.
The big vial on the plinth, the tour that starts by itself (X to close, explore on my own), personal next steps, booking and email capture.
Home, Programs (catalogue conveyor), The Lab, Pricing, Journal (The PEPTICITY Letter), FAQ, Contact, with the approved hooks wired in (preview mode) and tilt-lift cards everywhere.
The redesigned docked guide bar, expanded vetted answers from the peptide skills, and a red-team test suite.
Quality gate, accessibility, speed budgets, a compliance pass and the counsel question list, then an award-jury score of 8/10 or better before you see the finished build.
'What we fixed' list for Grace, counsel questions, domain and hosting, real form connections, privacy-safe analytics, award submission kit.
